what: Which modifications were applied, and which were not
title: Digesting and fragmenting peptidoforms
text: mzLib loads UniProt feature types. census says many annotations applied, rest :
code: census_explain(digest) #> [1] "14 of 38 annotated modifications were applied, across 14 residue positions. Excluded by type: 24 x glycosylation site - mzLib loads only 'modified residue' and 'lipid moiety-binding region' annotations, so these were dropped on feature type alone. The exclusion is usually right: a glycation or glycosylation annotation describes a labile, heterogeneous adduct, so assigning it one exact mass and a clean fragment ladder would invent a species you cannot observe. But the reason is not reported, and the qualifier is not read - some annotations are marked 'in vitro' and some exist only in disease variants, which are different grounds for exclusion needing different judgements from you. Read the annotations on the UniProt entry before concluding anything about a specific site; this census can only tell you the count (smith-chem-wisc/mzLib#1112)." head(census_excluded(digest)) #> [1] 24

code: check_download <- function(path, expected) { # NA when the file is the one PRIDE recorded, otherwise what is wrong with it. size <- file.size(path) if (size != expected$size_bytes) { return(paste(size, "bytes where PRIDE records", expected$size_bytes)) } md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(path)) if (md5 != tolower(expected$md5)) { return(paste("MD5", md5, "where PRIDE records", expected$md5)) } NA_character_ } readme <- checksums["README.txt", ] damaged <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt") writeBin(charToRaw(strrep("x", 1000)), damaged) check_download(damaged, readme) #> [1] "1000 bytes where PRIDE records 1645" error_page <- "ConnectionClosedException" writeBin(charToRaw(paste0(error_page, strrep(".", 1645 - nchar(error_page)))), damaged) check_download(damaged, readme) #> [1] "MD5 6a8f1a7d39089d34bf9bc9b19e553dd4 where PRIDE records 492753137013825025e6729c8798664f" # Not run: downloads files from PRIDE. paths <- pride_download("PXD000001", "downloads", category = "RAW") checksums <- pride_file_checksums("PXD000001") for (path in paths) { name <- basename(path) if (!name %in% rownames(checksums)) { message(name, ": PRIDE has no checksum for it, so it cannot be checked") next } problem <- check_download(path, checksums[name, ]) if (!is.na(problem)) message(name, ": ", problem, ". Download it again.") }

code: # Not run: needs your MetaMorpheus search output. psms <- readers_read_records("AllPSMs.psmtsv")$records peptides <- readers_read_quantified_peptides("AllQuantifiedPeptides.tsv")$records  # Intensity per (run, full sequence), MS/MS-detected only. FlashLFQ's 0 means "not quantified". msms <- peptides[peptides$detection_type == "MSMS" & !is.na(peptides$intensity) & peptides$intensity > 0, ] intensity <- setNames(msms$intensity, paste(msms$sample_label, msms$sequence, sep = "\r"))  # MetaMorpheus writes one value when every protein shares it, else one per protein. per_protein <- function(cell, count) {   parts <- strsplit(cell, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]   if (length(parts) == 1L) rep(parts, count) else parts }  # Your choice of PSMs: targets, q-value below 1%, one unambiguous peptidoform. kept <- psms[psms$decoy_contam_target == "T" & psms$q_value < 0.01 & psms$ambiguity_level == "1", ] rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(kept)), function(i) {   p <- kept[i, ]   accessions <- strsplit(p$protein_accession, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]   spans <- per_protein(p$start_and_end_residues_in_parent_sequence, length(accessions))  # "[69 to 84]"   before <- per_protein(p$previous_residue, length(accessions))   ends <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(gsub("[][]", "", spans), " to ", fixed = TRUE))   data.frame(run = p$file_name_without_extension, full_sequence = p$full_sequence,              protein_accession = accessions, start_residue = as.integer(ends[, 1]),              end_residue = as.integer(ends[, 2]), previous_residue = ifelse(nchar(before) == 1, before, "")) })) rows <- unique(rows) rows$intensity <- unname(intensity[paste(rows$run, rows$full_sequence, sep = "\r")]) write.table(rows[, c("run", "full_sequence", "protein_accession", "start_residue", "end_residue",                      "intensity", "previous_residue")],             "observations.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, na = "")

title: SDRF-Proteomics experimental designs
text: SDRF document row-major, data.frame, two reasons real: Column names repeat. comment[modification parameters] legitimately appears per modification, name identifies position, column. Rows can ragged. row may carry fewer cells header names, mzLib keeps file round-trips. columns character vector may repeat, rows list character vectors, accessors looking : NA sdrf_value() means document column, row short reach . reserved words "available" "applicable" different: values experiment chose write, come back . data.frame want, sdrf_records() gives one - lossy name repeats, sdrf_has_repeated_columns() tells first: ragged document, mzLib’s fixtures:
code: doc <- sdrf_read("PXD000070.sdrf.tsv") doc #> <mzlibr_sdrf> PXD000070.sdrf.tsv #>   31 columns (some names repeat - use sdrf_all()) #>   6 rows in the document, 6 returned #>   ! Cells are RAW STRINGS, never interpreted. The SDRF key=value grammar ("NT=Oxidation;AC=UNIMOD:35") is left exactly as written, because it cannot be told apart from a cell that merely contains '=' and ';' - comment[file uri] routinely carries pre-signed URLs that do. #>   ! column_names is a LIST, not a set: names may repeat, and their order is part of the document. comment[modification parameters] legitimately appears many times in one file, so a name identifies a POSITION rather than a column. #>   ! An SDRF reserved word - "not available", "not applicable" - is a real value meaning the experiment stated an absence. It is NOT the same as a column the document does not have, and the two must not be collapsed. sdrf_value(doc, "characteristics[organism part]") #> [1] "human erythrocytes" "human erythrocytes" "human erythrocytes" #> [4] "human erythrocytes" "human erythrocytes" "human erythrocytes" sdrf_indexes_of(doc, "comment[modification parameters]") #> [1] 20 21 22 23 24 25 26 27 sdrf_all(doc, "comment[modification parameters]")[[1]] #> [1] "NT=Carbamidomethyl;AC=UNIMOD:4;TA=C;MT=Fixed"            #> [2] "NT=Oxidation;AC=UNIMOD:35;TA=M,W,H;MT=Variable"          #> [3] "NT=Acetyl;AC=UNIMOD:1;PP=Protein N-term;MT=Variable"     #> [4] "NT=Acetyl;AC=UNIMOD:1;TA=K;MT=Variable"                  #> [5] "NT=Ammonia-loss;AC=UNIMOD:385;TA=Q,C;MT=Variable"        #> [6] "NT=Glu->pyro-Glu;AC=UNIMOD:27;TA=E;MT=Variable"          #> [7] "NT=Deamidated;AC=UNIMOD:7;PP=Protein N-term;MT=Variable" #> [8] "NT=Phospho;AC=UNIMOD:21;TA=S,T,Y,A;MT=Variable" sdrf_has_repeated_columns(doc) #> [1] TRUE head(sdrf_records(doc)[, c("source name", "characteristics[organism]")]) #>   source name characteristics[organism] #> 1    Sample 1     plasmodium falciparum #> 2    Sample 2     plasmodium falciparum #> 3    Sample 3     plasmodium falciparum #> 4    Sample 4     plasmodium falciparum #> 5    Sample 5     plasmodium falciparum #> 6    Sample 6     plasmodium falciparum ragged <- sdrf_read("PXD059974.sdrf.tsv") sdrf_ragged_row_count(ragged) #> [1] 17

Columns union documents, cell document filled "available" - fill rate computed pooled table fill rate originals. pooled table analysis, deposit: two experiments may “Sample 1”, keep sdrf_source_documents() key. writes whole pooled document, whatever limit . mzLib adds .sdrf.tsv name already end , = "x.tsv" writes x.tsv.sdrf.tsv; written$path names file wrote. Name file .sdrf.tsv two agree:
code: pooled <- sdrf_pool(c(malaria = "PXD000070.sdrf.tsv", colon = "PXD026824.sdrf.tsv"), limit = 4) pooled #> <mzlibr_pooled_sdrf> 2 documents: malaria, colon #>   38 columns (some names repeat - use sdrf_all()) #>   24 rows in the document, 4 returned #>   ! truncated - rows were left behind #>   ! Every cell a source document did not have is filled with the reserved word "not available". Those words are therefore partly an artefact of pooling rather than something an experiment said, and a fill-rate computed over this table is not the fill rate of the originals. #>   ! Provenance is in the 'comment[source document]' column. It is stamped only where a source document had none, so pooling an already-pooled table keeps the inner labels rather than overwriting them. #>   ! This is an ANALYSIS table, not something to deposit. source name + assay name + comment[label] is unique within one document, but two experiments may both have a "Sample 1", so the pooled table will usually violate SDRF's uniqueness rule. Use the source-document column as part of any key. #>   ! Columns are the UNION over all 2 documents, ordered by SDRF's own block structure, and a name that repeats is carried at the highest multiplicity any single document used, so no values are dropped. sdrf_source_documents(pooled) #> [1] "malaria" "malaria" "malaria" "malaria" # Not run: writes a file, which the recordings this page replays did not. pooled <- sdrf_pool(c(malaria = "PXD000070.sdrf.tsv", colon = "PXD026824.sdrf.tsv"),                     out = "pooled.tsv") pooled$written$path   # ".../pooled.tsv.sdrf.tsv"

title: Differential abundance: limma's moderated t, contrasts, and the tests around it
text: mzLib’s test suite carries frozen limma run: 400 features, 12 samples missing values, design intercept, age decades sex, limma’s eBayes output age coefficient. package ships input limma’s output extdata/stats/: Compare every feature limma said: Every relative difference 1e-8. limma installed can run input, limma::eBayes(limma::lmFit(y, x), legacy = TRUE); package’s tests exactly , bh_adjusted p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"). limma: legacy estimator. matches eBayes(legacy = TRUE). features different residual degrees freedom, limma 3.61 later default different prior estimator. Omitting missing values per feature exactly makes residual df differ, label-free data default limma reports slightly different prior different moderated statistics. fit says input case:
code: data <- system.file("extdata", "stats", package = "mzLibR") fit <- stats_fit(file.path(data, "limma_reference_responses.tsv"),                  file.path(data, "limma_reference_design.tsv"), "age_decades") fit #> <mzlibr_moderated_fit> 400 features x 12 samples, testing age_decades #>   fitted 400, too_few_observations 0, rank_deficient 0 #>   prior df 4.532 (moments_legacy) #>   ! residual df differ between features: these are eBayes(legacy = TRUE) statistics fit$coefficient_names #> [1] "Intercept"   "age_decades" "sex" limma <- read.delim(file.path(data, "limma_ebayes_notrend.tsv")) worst <- function(ours, theirs) max(abs(ours - theirs) / abs(theirs)) c(t = worst(fit$records$t, limma$t_age),   p_value = worst(fit$records$p_value, limma$p_age),   bh_adjusted = worst(fit$records$bh_adjusted, limma$bh_age),   posterior_variance = worst(fit$records$posterior_variance, limma$s2_post),   df_total = worst(fit$records$df_total, limma$df_total)) #>                  t            p_value        bh_adjusted posterior_variance  #>       1.612212e-11       2.414497e-13       2.414120e-13       3.156851e-14  #>           df_total  #>       3.727223e-16 fit$residual_df_differ #> [1] TRUE

Halving MALAT1 read log2 fold change -1, quartering -2. responses oligo’s log2 FlashLFQ intensity minus run’s median log2 intensity FLuc-oligos (blank FlashLFQ detected nothing), one row per oligo named <transcript>:<sequence>. design intercept, coefficient change 500 ng runs: oligos fitted, fit says rather dropping . oligo seen two three runs residual variance estimate (too_few_observations); one seen 500 ng runs 250 ng effect (rank_deficient). rows NA statistics, neither enters Benjamini-Hochberg family. question experiment designed answer, median log2 fold change per transcript: Half MALAT1 reads -0.9 known -1; quarter reads -1 known -2. second compressed half. statistics create : estimates ordinary least squares, moderation changes standard errors. FLuc sits near 0 largely construction, since every run normalised . oligos pass 5% false discovery rate? , true. Two quarter-load calls 20-mer oligos, loaded constant amount. 5% false discovery rate bounds expected share wrong calls; promise none, known-answer experiment see happen.

title: What UniProt annotated, and what mzLib could actually use — census_explain
code: digest <- peptidoform_fragments("P02768", max_modifications = 1) census_explain(digest) #> [1] "14 of 38 annotated modifications were applied, across 14 residue positions. Excluded by type: 24 x glycosylation site - mzLib loads only 'modified residue' and 'lipid moiety-binding region' annotations, so these were dropped on feature type alone. The exclusion is usually right: a glycation or glycosylation annotation describes a labile, heterogeneous adduct, so assigning it one exact mass and a clean fragment ladder would invent a species you cannot observe. But the reason is not reported, and the qualifier is not read - some annotations are marked 'in vitro' and some exist only in disease variants, which are different grounds for exclusion needing different judgements from you. Read the annotations on the UniProt entry before concluding anything about a specific site; this census can only tell you the count (smith-chem-wisc/mzLib#1112)."

Present __fragments. secondary_product_type string; NA terminal ion (MslFragmentIon.SecondaryProductType null every terminal ion), fragment ions. internal ion's C-terminal ProductType, e.g. y bIy. Present __fragments. fragment_number int; NA precursor fragment ions. ion's number series, e.g. 5 b5; internal ion, 0-based start residue (MslFragmentIon.FragmentNumber). Present __fragments. secondary_fragment_number int; NA terminal ion, mzLib stores 0 (MslFragmentIon.SecondaryFragmentNumber), fragment ions. internal ion's end residue, exclusive. Present __fragments. fragment_charge int; charge; NA precursor fragment ions. Fragment charge (MslFragmentIon.Charge). Present __fragments. neutral_loss float; Da; NA precursor fragment ions. title: The conditions mzLibR signals, and how to handle each — mzlib_error
text: mzlib_usage_error - call malformed: missing invalid argument, file , file view. Raised work happens, either mzLibR bridge (usage kind, exit status 2). Fix call; retrying help. pyMzLib raises UsageError, mzLibRust returns MzLibError::Usage. mzlib_service_unavailable - external service , rate-limited, timing unreachable: HTTP 408, 429 5xx PRIDE, UniProt EBI. Retry later. PRIDE, mzLib already retried request three times, 5, 20 60 s (mzLib #1412), later means minutes, seconds. 404 400 deliberately class, wrong URL malformed request defect, excusing outage hide . Two PRIDE failures EBI's arrive mzlib_bridge_error error_type "HttpRequestException": FTP listing still empty, 403 EBI's FTP host, mzLib's retries. Treat outage. live tests skip class nothing else. pyMzLib raises ServiceUnavailableError. mzlib_bridge_error - mzLib reported failure (spec's correctness kind): file parse, vendor library load platform. error_type field carries .NET exception type, e.g. "HttpRequestException", handler can tell failures apart without parsing prose. pyMzLib raises BridgeError. mzlib_project_not_found - PRIDE project accession. PRIDE answers unknown accession empty list rather 404, empty list indistinguishable project nothing matching, raised rather returning list(). mzlib_timeout - bridge finish within timeout seconds. Deliberately mzlib_service_unavailable: timeout can mean slow service, equally wedged bridge, corrupt executable timeout set short, mzLibR guess . seconds field limit exceeded. mzlib_bridge_not_found - bridge executable located, run. message names three ways provide one; see mzlibr_install_bridge mzlibr_bridge_path. mzlib_protocol_error - bridge answered something version read: output process died (stderr quoted message), text JSON, wire protocol one mzLibR speaks. Usually bridge package different releases; mzlibr_bridge_version says .

Trimethylation lysine epsilon-amine gives quaternary ammonium, carries charge proton. UniProt records delta 43.054227 (C3H7 *minus electron*); mzLib loads one proton lighter, 42.046951 (C3H6), adding charge protons monoisotopic_mass gives right m/z. Adding full complement UniProt's mass put 2+ trimethylated peptide half Thomson high. fixed_charges deprecated always 0 pyMzLib 0.7.0 bridge, formula adds charge protons. still subtracts fixed_charges, keeps m/z right digest older bridge, whose monoisotopic_mass carried UniProt's charged mass: m/z either. text: accession UniProt accession, e.g. "P02768" (serum albumin). protease protease name, mzLib names . NULL means mzLib's default protease. Read coming MaxQuant Mascot. names one cuts   mzLib's. mzLib's "trypsin" cuts K R even proline, "trypsin|P"   cut proline: P names residue prevents cut.   reverse MaxQuant's Mascot's Trypsin/P, ignores proline rule. serum   albumin two give 202 195 distinct peptides, small count hiding large   difference: peptides get changes wherever K R precedes proline   (smith-chem-wisc/mzLib#1106). dissociation "HCD" "CID" (b y ions), "ETD", "ECD", rest   mzLib's dissociation types. NULL means "HCD": mzLib names default , HCD   bridge's choice mzLib names one (smith-chem-wisc/mzLib#1488). "ETD" "ECD" return c z-dot series, c zDot (radical N-Ca   cleavage yields c/z-dot, b/y vibrational activation). mzLib PR #1114 removed   spurious y series ETD used emit. modifications Whether apply UniProt's annotated modifications. FALSE gives bare sequences - clean control, since digest's distinct backbones   unchanged modified variants go away. peptidoform count drops   long way; albumin 310 202. carried caveat saying FALSE also discarded proteolysis products,   peptide list changed albumin lost two signal-peptide peptides   (smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib#8). true longer: peptides present   either way, albumin gives 202 distinct base sequences modifications . missed_cleavages Maximum missed cleavage sites per peptide. NULL means mzLib's   default. min_length Shortest peptide keep, residues. NULL means mzLib's default. mzLib's default silently discards everything shorter. Albumin goes 202 distinct   sequences default 257 min_length = 1 - fifth digest lives   - histone H3.1 keeps 49 96 peptides, start end, gives   min_length = 1. looking short peptide finding , look   first, pass min_length = 1 mean every peptide. max_length Longest peptide keep, residues. NULL means mzLib's default,   unbounded; 0 asks bound. max_modifications Maximum modifications considered per peptide. NULL means mzLib's   default. Modification isoforms enumerated combinatorially: histone H3.1's 49 peptides   give 2,419 peptidoforms two modifications 6,580 three. max_isoforms Maximum modification isoforms (peptidoforms) generated per peptide   position. NULL means mzLib's default. cap truncates silently. truncated result genuinely short one look   identical outside - histone H3.1 four modifications default cap keeps   8,644 12,808 peptidoforms, losing third. code: # mzLib's own deletion case: QRQ (source 9 to 11) is missing from the target. aln <- proteins_align(list(c("MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ", "MKTAYIAKISFVKSHFSRQ"))) aln #> <mzlibr_alignments> 1 pair(s), global-affine;BLOSUM62;open=11;extend=1;end-gaps=free #>   pair 1: score 80 half-bits, 19 identical, 0 substituted, 3 + 0 facing a gap #>   residue map: 41 rows; NA mapped_position faces a gap writeLines(c(aln$records$aligned_source, aln$records$aligned_target)) #> MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ #> MKTAYIAK---ISFVKSHFSRQ aln$records[, c("score", "identical", "source_residues_facing_gap")] #>   score identical source_residues_facing_gap #> 1    80        19                          3 proteins_map_source_to_target(aln, 8:12) #> [1]  8 NA NA NA  9  # Two pairs in one call; the free overhang MLLL faces a gap. alns <- proteins_align(list(c("MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ", "MKTAYIAKISFVKSHFSRQ"),                             c("MLLLPEPTIDE", "PEPTIDE"))) alns$records[, c("pair_index", "score", "aligned_target")] #>   pair_index score         aligned_target #> 1          1    80 MKTAYIAK---ISFVKSHFSRQ #> 2          2    39            ----PEPTIDE proteins_map_source_to_target(proteins_alignments(alns)[[2]], 1:5) #> [1] NA NA NA NA  1  # Charging the end gaps changes the overhang's score, and the aligner id says so: charged <- proteins_align(list(c("MLLLPEPTIDE", "PEPTIDE")), end_gaps = "charged") charged$records$score #> [1] 24 charged$aligner_id #> [1] "global-affine;BLOSUM62;open=11;extend=1;end-gaps=charged"

code: # mzLib's own test world: four human genes, three mouse and two rat, with every human-mouse # row in the mouse dump, as in release 116. gtfs <- c(homo_sapiens = "Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gtf",           mus_musculus = "Mus_musculus.GRCm39.116.gtf",           rattus_norvegicus = "Rattus_norvegicus.GRCr8.116.gtf") dumps <- paste0("homologies/", names(gtfs), "/Compara.116.protein_default.homologies.tsv.gz") snap <- proteins_build_orthology("116", gtfs = gtfs, dumps = dumps,   gene_trees = "vertebrates.GeneTree_content.default.e116.txt.gz",   pair_status = c("homo_sapiens", "mus_musculus")) snap #> <mzlibr_orthology_snapshot> Ensembl 116, 3 species: homo_sapiens, mus_musculus, rattus_norvegicus #>   snapshot_id 5487ebcabe48... (record it with any result) #>   orthologs: homo_sapiens~mus_musculus 3, homo_sapiens~rattus_norvegicus 1, mus_musculus~rattus_norvegicus 2 #>   homo_sapiens in mus_musculus: has_ortholog 2, tree_lacks_target_species 1, not_in_any_tree 1 #>   ! The dumps of homo_sapiens, mus_musculus, rattus_norvegicus share the file name Compara.116.protein_default.homologies.tsv.gz, and the pairs tables' source_dump column holds only the file name, so it cannot say which species' dump a row came from. manifest.json's inputs list each dump with its species and sha256. #>   ! The gene trees were read unrestricted: 9 genes were held in memory, 8 of them in the given gene sets. --restrict-gene-trees holds only those and gives the same snapshot. snap$pair_status$records[, c("gene_id", "gene_biotype", "status")] #>           gene_id   gene_biotype                    status #> 1 ENSG00000000001 protein_coding              has_ortholog #> 2 ENSG00000000002 protein_coding              has_ortholog #> 3 ENSG00000000003 protein_coding tree_lacks_target_species #> 4 ENSG00000000004 protein_coding           not_in_any_tree snap$dumps[, c("species", "rows_kept")] #>             species rows_kept #> 1      homo_sapiens         1 #> 2      mus_musculus         5 #> 3 rattus_norvegicus         1 proteins_orthology_pair(snap, "mus_musculus", "homo_sapiens")$row_count #> [1] 3  # With out = the snapshot is written, and its id is the same: written <- proteins_build_orthology("116", gtfs = gtfs, dumps = dumps,   gene_trees = "vertebrates.GeneTree_content.default.e116.txt.gz",   restrict_gene_trees = TRUE, out = "compara-116") identical(written$snapshot_id, snap$snapshot_id) #> [1] TRUE head(written$written$files[, c("path", "rows")], 7) #>                                       path rows #> 1               genes/homo_sapiens.parquet    4 #> 2               genes/mus_musculus.parquet    3 #> 3          genes/rattus_norvegicus.parquet    2 #> 4             members/homo_sapiens.parquet    3 #> 5             members/mus_musculus.parquet    3 #> 6        members/rattus_norvegicus.parquet    2 #> 7 pairs/homo_sapiens__homo_sapiens.parquet    0

code: # Two modifications on one molecule, mzLib's PhysicalPairsCarryCoOccupancy case: cases <- system.file("extdata", "ptmqtl", "cases.tsv", package = "mzLibR") found <- ptmqtl_pairs(cases, type = "physical") found$records[, c("site_a", "statistic", "n", "statistic_n", "p_value")] #>                                              site_a statistic n statistic_n #> 1 TWO_ON_ONE:K14:Common Biological:Acetylation on K      0.25 2           1 #>   p_value #> 1      NA  # Twelve runs in two batches, every site 0.2 higher in the second. The batch alone correlates # two sites; given each run's level, they are unrelated: batch <- system.file("extdata", "ptmqtl", "batch.tsv", package = "mzLibR") plain <- ptmqtl_pairs(batch, type = "covarying") given <- ptmqtl_pairs(batch, type = "covarying", remove_run_level = TRUE) pick <- function(r) r$statistic[startsWith(r$site_a, "PAIR_S") & startsWith(r$site_b, "PAIR_T")] round(c(plain = pick(plain$records), given = pick(given$records)), 2) #> plain given  #>  0.76  0.03

One row here is one CHARGE STATE of one feature, not one row of the file. mzLib expands each deconvolved feature across [ChargeStateMin, ChargeStateMax] (Ms1Feature.cs:84), so record_count exceeds the file's line count, and a charge the tool never observed appears if the writer recorded a gapped charge range. Use read-records for the file's own rows. #>   ! intensity is the per-charge APEX intensity (Ms1Feature.cs:86), not the summed intensity over the feature. The file's own Intensity column is a different number, and read-records has it. #>   ! retention_time_start/_end are in UNKNOWN units for this format. TopFD wrote seconds through v1.6.2 and minutes from v1.7.0 without changing the file type, and mzLib normalises neither - its deconvolution parameters instead GUESS, dividing by 60 when the largest end time exceeds 500. Check the values against your gradient length before comparing them with anything. #>   ! number_of_isotopes is null for every row of this format: the single-charge expansion mzLib builds never sets it (Ms1Feature.cs:91). code: matches <- readers_read_matches("PXD078927_msgf_1_1_0.mzid", limit = 3) matches #> <mzlibr_match_records> C:\Users\trish\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\E--CodeReview-bridge\eebe6abc-2c7e-4422-9d4e-f0aaa03b3152\scratchpad\wt_c1\code\mzLib\mzLib\Test\DataFiles\PXD078927_msgf_1_1_0.mzid (MzIdentML) #>   12 records in the file, 3 returned #>   ! truncated - records were left behind #>   ! NOTHING here is FDR-filtered. q_value is the only confidence field this view carries, and only mzIdentML and an MsPathFinderT file with a QValue column fill it (absent_fields says when it is empty). Every one of these formats records scores this view does not expose; read-records has them. Filter before you report. #>   ! is_decoy is null for this format. mzIdentML's isDecoy attribute is optional and defaults to false, and mzLib reports a decoy only when every peptide evidence says so (MzIdentMLResultFile.cs:189), so false cannot be told apart from 'not stated'. read-records carries mzLib's boolean for a caller who knows the writer sets it. #>   ! Every SpectrumIdentificationItem is a row, not only the matches the submitter accepted: lower-ranked candidates and items that fail the threshold are here too (MzIdentMLResultFile.cs:193). Filter on rank == 1 and pass_threshold before counting identifications. #>   ! one_based_scan_number is parsed from the nativeID (MzIdentMLResultFile.cs:175). 'scan=N' gives N, but 'index=N', which peak-list input carries, is a zero-based position in the file and gives N + 1, not an instrument scan number. -1 means the nativeID had neither. #>   ! Items mzLib cannot represent as one linear match are skipped, not failed: crosslinks, modifications without a resolvable UNIMOD accession, substitutions, and two modifications on one residue (MzIdentMLResultFile.cs:123). They are not rows; skipped_count and skipped name each one and why, so record_count plus skipped_count is the number of items in the file. #>   ! The engine's own scores (for example MS-GF:SpecEValue) have no common name across search engines (MzIdentMLResultFile.cs:195). Pass scores=true for them as long rows, one per match and score. q_value is null on an item that reports none. #>   ! accession joins every protein the item's peptide evidence names with '|' (MzIdentMLRecord.cs:45), the same character a UniProt header uses inside one accession, so the cell cannot be split back into proteins reliably. #>   absent from this file (NA in every row): is_decoy matches$records[, c("one_based_scan_number", "base_sequence", "q_value", "rank")] #>   one_based_scan_number  base_sequence   q_value rank #> 1                 14316   HSNLNDATYQRT 0.0000000    1 #> 2                 14316 KASAGQISVQPTFS 0.6588785    2 #> 3                 14316   TRQYTADNLNSH 0.7383230    3  # One row per match and engine score: scored <- readers_read_matches("PXD078927_msgf_1_1_0.mzid", limit = 1, scores = TRUE) scored$records[, c("match_index", "score_name", "score_value")] #>   match_index        score_name  score_value #> 1           0    MS-GF:RawScore 1.150000e+02 #> 2           0 MS-GF:DeNovoScore 1.230000e+02 #> 3           0  MS-GF:SpecEValue 3.041116e-14 #> 4           0      MS-GF:EValue 8.393480e-12 #> 5           0      MS-GF:QValue 0.000000e+00 #> 6           0   MS-GF:PepQValue 0.000000e+00 #> 7           0      IsotopeError 1.000000e+00  # Casanovo writes no target/decoy label, so is_decoy is NA rather than a false FALSE. denovo <- readers_read_matches("Casanovo_5.0.0.mztab") denovo$absent_fields #> [1] "is_decoy"       "q_value"        "rank"           "pass_threshold"

Cells are RAW STRINGS, never interpreted. The SDRF key=value grammar ("NT=Oxidation;AC=UNIMOD:35") is left exactly as written, because it cannot be told apart from a cell that merely contains '=' and ';' - comment[file uri] routinely carries pre-signed URLs that do. #>   ! column_names is a LIST, not a set: names may repeat, and their order is part of the document. comment[modification parameters] legitimately appears many times in one file, so a name identifies a POSITION rather than a column. #>   ! An SDRF reserved word - "not available", "not applicable" - is a real value meaning the experiment stated an absence. It is NOT the same as a column the document does not have, and the two must not be collapsed. sdrf_value(doc, "characteristics[organism]") #> [1] "plasmodium falciparum" "plasmodium falciparum" "plasmodium falciparum" #> [4] "plasmodium falciparum" "plasmodium falciparum" "plasmodium falciparum"

title: Restrict an SDRF to the files one search read, and report what could not be placed — sdrf_restrict
code: # Two calibrated runs, the raw file of one of them as well, a renamed file whose acquisition you # know, and one the SDRF does not describe: pool1 <- "HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr0" pool5 <- "HJOSLO2U_QEHF_20150329_TMT_pool5_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr0" searched <- c(paste0("D:\\search\\", pool1, "1-calib.mzML"), paste0(pool1, "2-calib.mzML"),   paste0(pool1, "2.raw"), "sample_A.mzML", "not_in_sdrf.mzML") names(searched) <- c("", "", "", paste0(pool5, "1.raw"), "") scoped <- sdrf_restrict("PXD008841.subset.sdrf.tsv", searched, limit = 2) scoped #> <mzlibr_restricted_sdrf> PXD008841.subset.sdrf.tsv: 30 of 40 rows kept for 5 searched file(s) #>   32 columns (some names repeat - use sdrf_all()) #>   30 rows in the document, 2 returned #>   ! truncated - rows were left behind #>   ! The join is by STEM, case-insensitively, after mzLib removes MetaMorpheus's derivative suffixes (-calib, -averaged, in any order and number), so X-calib.mzML finds the row naming X.raw. A searched<TAB>acquired line overrides that rule for its file. A row whose stem joins nothing is tried once more by an earlier search's comment[searched data file]. #>   ! Kept rows are carried cell for cell: no replicate or fraction is renumbered. mzLib adds comment[searched data file] (the searched file's name, no folder) directly after comment[data file], and replaces one an earlier search wrote. #>   ! A kept row shorter than the header is padded with empty cells, so this document is never ragged, unlike what sdrf read returns for the same file. #>   ! ambiguous: two or more searched files claimed one acquisition; the first in name order kept it, and the others get no row and are not in searched_without_row. shared_stem: one searched file joined rows naming two or more DIFFERENT acquired files (X.raw and X.mzML); every such row is kept, so the document can describe one run twice, and only the depositor can say which is right. A row naming no file is dropped without being listed in dropped_data_files. #>   ! The design verbs match searched files by EXACT name. Restrict first: sdrf design and sdrf isobaric-design key on comment[searched data file] when a document has it, so the restricted document joins the search's own file names. #>   ! --out writes the WHOLE restricted document, whatever limit and offset are, through mzLib's SdrfDocument.WriteResults: atomically, with CRLF line endings whatever the input used. mzLib adds .sdrf.tsv to a name that does not already end in it, so written.path is the file actually written. #>   searched without a row: not_in_sdrf.mzML #>   acquired but not searched: HJOSLO2U_QEHF_20150329_TMT_pool5_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02.raw #>   ambiguous: HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02: HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02-calib.mzML, HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02.raw c(input = scoped$input_row_count, kept = scoped$row_count, returned = scoped$returned_count) #>    input     kept returned  #>       40       30        2  sdrf_searched_data_files(scoped) #> [1] "HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr01-calib.mzML" #> [2] "HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr01-calib.mzML" scoped$searched_without_row #> [1] "not_in_sdrf.mzML" scoped$dropped_data_files #> [1] "HJOSLO2U_QEHF_20150329_TMT_pool5_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02.raw" writeLines(strwrap(scoped$ambiguous, 80)) #> HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02: #> HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02-calib.mzML, #> HJOS2U_20140410_TMTpool1_300ugIPG37-49_7of15ul_fr02.raw

code: # A dilution series from mzLib's own RNA test data: MALAT1 at 500, 250 and 125 ng against a # constant FLuc spike, log2 intensities normalised to FLuc. Halving MALAT1 should read as about -1. data <- system.file("extdata", "stats", package = "mzLibR") fit <- stats_fit(file.path(data, "malat_dilution_log2_vs_fluc.tsv"),   file.path(data, "malat_dilution_design.tsv"), c("malat_250ng", "malat_125ng")) fit #> <mzlibr_moderated_fit> 492 features x 27 samples, testing malat_250ng, malat_125ng #>   fitted 212, too_few_observations 214, rank_deficient 66 #>   prior df 19.56 (moments_legacy) #>   ! residual df differ between features: these are eBayes(legacy = TRUE) statistics fit$status_counts #>               fitted too_few_observations       rank_deficient  #>                  212                  214                   66  c(estimator = fit$prior$estimator, prior_df = round(fit$prior$df, 1)) #>        estimator         prior_df  #> "moments_legacy"           "19.6"  malat <- fit$records[fit$records$coefficient == "malat_250ng" & fit$records$status == "fitted" &   startsWith(fit$records$feature, "MALAT1:"), ] c(oligos = nrow(malat), median_log2_fold_change = median(malat$estimate)) #>                  oligos median_log2_fold_change  #>             116.0000000              -0.8914901   # Every pair of loads, with intervals: diff_design() with no reference level writes one contrast # per pair beside the design, and `contrasts` tests them all. samples <- system.file("extdata", "diff", "malat_dilution_samples.tsv", package = "mzLibR") design <- diff_design(samples, factors = list(factor_spec("malat_load")),   out = file.path(tempdir(), "malat_pairs")) stratum <- design$strata[[1]] pairs <- stats_fit(file.path(data, "malat_dilution_log2_vs_fluc.tsv"), stratum$design_file,   contrasts = stratum$contrasts_file) pairs$contrasts #> <mzlibr_moderated_contrasts> 3 contrast(s) x 492 features, 95% intervals #>   c1: 0 1 0 #>   c2: 0 0 1 #>   c3:  0 -1  1 pairs$contrasts$weights$c3 #> [1]  0 -1  1 pairs$coefficient_names #> [1] "intercept"        "malat_load=250ng" "malat_load=500ng"
